newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish labour board sees June jobless 9.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish labour board sees June jobless 9.4 pct.

text.p: Swedish unemployment was 9.4 percent in June compared with 7.6 percent in May, Sweden's Labour Market Board (AMS) said on Friday.
A total of 413,00 people were unemployed during the month, which was 92,000 more than in May this year but 6,000 fewer than in June last year.
The increase in unemployment between June and May was seasonal, the board said in a statement.

This figure, which excludes people in government sponsored jobs or training schemes, depends partly on how many people put themselves down as looking for work and this number tends to decline in the summer.
In June 31,500 new jobs were advertised in the labour market which was an increase of 1,500 from May and 5,500 more than in June last year.
The labour board is one of two sources of Swedish unemployment figures.
The other, Sweden's official statistics bureau, Statistics Sweden, will release its unemployment figures for June at 1100 GMT on July 11.
Statistics Sweden said 7.8 percent of people were unemployed in May compared with the labour board's figure of 7.6 percent.
